english.title: Racially / religiously aggravated harassment without violence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) pursued a course of conduct which amounted to the harassment of **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) and which you knew or ought to have known amounted to the harassment of

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

in that **(..SPECIFY THE DATES, PLACES AND NATURE OF CONDUCT..), and the offence was

(C)_[racially]_
(D)_[religiously]_

aggravated within the terms of section 28 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32(1)(a) and (3) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 and section 2 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The option to return an alternative verdict of guilty of the basic offence is not available in the magistrates court, therefore the basic offence should be charged in addition to the aggravated offence.
(ii) See offence wording H5 for note re. conduct required pursuant to section 7 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
(iii) The conduct must have taken place on at least two occasions on or after 30 September 1998.
(iv) If, on trial on indictments of a person charged with this offence, the jury find him not guilty of the offence charged, they may find him guilty of the basic offence in section 2 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
